chain.title: Blank Module
chain.desc: Paper, redstone and gold nuggets, six at a time. Every module in the mod is this card plus one identifying ingredient.

chain.title: Modular Router
chain.desc: Iron ingots and iron bars around a Blank Module. One block that holds nine modules, three upgrades, a buffer slot and a redstone mode.

chain.title: Blank Upgrade
chain.desc: Paper, lapis and gold nuggets. The second base card - modules define what a router does, upgrades define how well.

chain.title: Puller Module Mk1
chain.desc: A sticky piston plus a Blank Module. It reaches into the inventory the router is facing and drags items into the buffer.

chain.title: Sender Module Mk1
chain.desc: A piston plus a Blank Module. The outbound half: it pushes from the buffer into a target inventory a short distance away.

chain.title: Speed Upgrade
chain.desc: Blaze rods, gunpowder, gold and redstone around a Blank Upgrade. Routers tick slowly by default; this is the first thing you will want more of.

chain.title: Stack Upgrade
chain.desc: Bricks and stone bricks around a Blank Upgrade. Each one raises how many items a module moves per operation, from one toward a full stack.

chain.title: Augment Core
chain.desc: One Blank Module plus one Blank Upgrade, four at a time. The third base card - augments slot into a single module instead of the router.

chain.title: Bulk Item Filter
chain.desc: Diamonds, iron and glass around a Blank Module. Holds far more entries than a module's own filter slots and is the parent of every other filter.

chain.title: Detector Module
chain.desc: A comparator plus a Blank Module; it makes the router emit a redstone signal based on what is in its buffer.

chain.title: Breaker Module
chain.desc: Break the block in front of the router and drop it into the buffer, respecting tool enchantments carried in the module's own slot.

chain.title: Placer Module
chain.desc: A dispenser and dirt plus a Blank Module; the inverse of the breaker - it plants what is in the buffer into the world.

chain.title: Activator Module
chain.desc: A dispenser, a lever, quartz and redstone around a Blank Module. It right-clicks for you: shearing, bonemealing, eating, firing bows.

chain.title: Vacuum Module
chain.desc: A hopper and an eye of ender plus a Blank Module; it sucks loose item entities out of the air into the router.

chain.title: Dropper Module
chain.desc: A dropper plus a Blank Module; spit buffer contents into the world as item entities rather than into an inventory.

chain.title: Flinger Module
chain.desc: Gunpowder plus a Dropper Module; the same idea with force and an aim vector, which is how you shoot items across a base.

chain.title: Extruder Module Mk2
chain.desc: A wooden chest plus a Blank Module. It lays a line of blocks out from the router and can pull them back in, building and unbuilding bridges on a redstone pulse.

chain.title: Fluid Module Mk1
chain.desc: A cauldron and glass around a Blank Module; routers stop being item-only and start moving buckets' worth of fluid.

chain.title: Fluid Upgrade
chain.desc: A bucket and glass around a Blank Upgrade; it raises the router's internal tank so fluid modules have somewhere to put what they pull.

chain.title: Energy Output Module
chain.desc: A redstone block, gold and quartz around a Blank Module; it pushes FE out of the router into adjacent machines.

chain.title: Energy Upgrade
chain.desc: The same materials on a Blank Upgrade; it gives the router an FE buffer, which the energy modules need to have anything to push.

chain.title: Sender Module Mk2
chain.desc: An ender pearl plus a Mk1 Sender. Mk2 drops the line-of-sight requirement and works to any block in range.

chain.title: Sender Module Mk3
chain.desc: End stone and an ender chest plus a Mk2. Unlimited range within a dimension - this is where a router stops being a hopper and starts being a network.

chain.title: Distributor Module
chain.desc: A Blank Module and a Mk2 Sender; it splits one input across many targets instead of filling the first one it finds.

chain.title: Player Module
chain.desc: A wither skeleton skull, diamond helmet and chestplate with a Mk2 Puller and a Mk3 Sender. It reads and writes a named player's own inventory, ender chest or armour slots.

notes: THE MODULES ARE THE CONTENT. There is exactly ONE block in this mod - modularrouters:modular_router - and 51 cards. A router does nothing until you put modules in it, so the whole progression is horizontal: three base cards (blank_module, blank_upgrade, augment_core) fan out into 20 modules, 10 upgrades, 12 augments and 5 filters. The chain quests the base cards and the modules that unlock genuinely new verbs; the wheels carry the families. 50 of 52 items are quested; the other 2 are dropped as unobtainable. TWO RECIPES ARE REGISTERED IN CODE AND WOULD BE MISSED BY A JSON-RESULT SCAN. data/modularrouters/recipes/breaker_module.json and extruder_module_1.json contain nothing but {"type": "modularrouters:<item>", "category": "misc"} - the ingredients and the result live in a custom recipe serializer named after the item, so a scanner looking for a 'result' key finds none and would wrongly mark both unobtainable. Both ARE craftable; the JSON file plus the matching serializer is the proof. extruder_module_1 is placed in the module wheel and breaker_module in the chain on that basis, and the breaker's description avoids naming a shape because the jar does not contain one. DROPPED AS UNOBTAINABLE: modularrouters:creative_module - modelled and named ('Creative Module', backed by CreativeModule.class) but there is no recipe anywhere in the jar; it is a creative-tab item. modularrouters:override_card - modelled and named 'Security Override Card' with no recipe, no loot table and no class of its own; it is an operator item handed out by command. NOT ITEMS, correctly excluded: modularrouters:manual has an item model and a texture but NO item.modularrouters.manual lang key - the only manual strings are modularrouters.patchouli.book.name / .landing, so the in-game manual is a patchouli:guide_book with NBT and the model is only its icon; questing 'modularrouters:manual' would be uncompletable. modularrouters:template_frame has a blockstate, a block model, a block lang key and TemplateFrameBlock.class but no item model and no recipe - it is the ghost block the Extruder Module places, not something you can hold. modularrouters:distributor_module_pull is a predicate override model on the distributor. A NAIVE LANG PASS ALSO OVERCOUNTS: item.modularrouters.range_upgrade and item.modularrouters.rangedown_upgrade are stale keys with no model, no class and no recipe - the live items are range_up_augment and range_down_augment. VERIFICATION: pass 1 strict models INTERSECT lang gave 52. Pass 2 re-derived the set independently from .class constant-pool strings, item textures, blockstates, recipe results and loot tables - all 52 corroborated; the only thing pass 2 surfaced that pass 1 had not claimed was template_frame, correctly excluded above. NO CONSENSUS DATA: moddb.json has no modularrouters entry, so ordering is the recipe dependency graph alone (blank_module -> router; the Mk1/Mk2/Mk3 sender and Mk1/Mk2 puller lines each consume the tier below; player_module genuinely consumes puller_module_2 AND sender_module_3, which is why it is last). Jar confirmed 1.20.1 Forge: META-INF/mods.toml, modId modularrouters, version 12.1.1+mc1.20.1, minecraft versionRange [1.20.1,), Java 17 class files, no fabric.mod.json.
